reason: This text (Exodus 17:1-7) describes the Israelites facing natural hardship (lack of water in the wilderness) and internal crisis rather than oppression or persecution as a people. The narrative shows the community complaining about deprivation and testing their faith, which prompts divine intervention. However, there is no indication of systematic oppression by external forces or persecutors. The people are not being oppressed or persecuted; rather, they are enduring wilderness trials and grappling with doubt. Oppression and persecution typically refer to external subjugation or hostile treatment by oppressors, which is not present in this passage.
